cultural.vision_reason: This is a mina'i enamel-painted ceramic beaker from Seljuq Kashan, Iran, showing seated courtly figures—Persian-made ceramic, but the claimed category "painting-mss" is wrong (it's a ceramic vessel).

physical.title: Mina'i Beaker with Seated Princes
physical.medium_raw: Fritware with overglaze design, mina’i ware
physical.summary: Mina’i ware takes its name from the Persian word for enamel. It was a luxurious type of pottery and used enamel painting to create true polychrome ceramic for the first time. Mina’i ware frequently combines blues, greens, and purples with sharp black and red executed with precise control. Figural scenes are quite common for these vessels and often recall book illustrations including rows of seated court members, sometimes flanking an enthroned ruler, and princely scenes of hunting or falconry.

location.made_in_place: Iran, Kashan, Seljuq period of Iran (1037–1194)
